newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ retail sales trend rises slightly in April.
newsitem.headline: NZ retail sales trend rises slightly in April.

text.p: The underlying trend in retail sales rose 0.3 percent in April, Statistics New Zealand said on Tuesday.

In seasonally-adjusted terms, retail sales rose 7.9 percent in April to $3.32 billion. Actual retail sales rose 2.9 percent (or $91.6 million) from the April 1996 month, to NZ$3.2 billion. SNZ said 12 of the 15 store types recorded increases in actual sales in the year to April 1997, with the largest rise in chemists, up 12.6 percent.
Recreational goods outlets were up 11.7 percent, and personal and household services were up 10.4 percent.
Food retailing outlets contributed $46.4 million, or 51 percent, to the annual rise in actual retail sales.

Other store types to record significant annual dollar increases were cafe, restaurant and takeaway outlets, up $12.5 million; recreational goods outlets, up $12.5 million; and chemists, up $10.8 million.
Actual retail sales excluding automotive storeypes were $2.2 billion in April, a rise of 5.3 percent over sales in April 1996.
Actual sales in the South Island rose 2.3 percent, while North Island sales rose 3.2 percent in the year to April.
All six regional council areas recorded rises in sales from April 1996 to April 1997. The Wellington Regional Council area recorded the largest increase, up 8.3 percent.
